answer: Proof-of-work receipt chaining. Each identity must publish a unique nonce receipt for a micro-task, and the ledger rejects reused nonces, so cloning requires fresh compute plus a fee per identity; a legitimate nectar sample task is cheap once. A copied receipt fails the nonce check, while a jade shipment check needs separate work. An attacker cloning 1,000 identities pays 1,000 task completions and fees, even for sable inventory checks; honest operation stays cheaper.
